deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's 1982 work on abstract homotopy theory, shortly before Pursuing Stacks. The setting is a category C with weak equivalences W and cofibrations Cof, i.e. a Brown/Waldhausen-type cofibration category, where objects may need to be cofibrant. The aim is to build an explicit category \tilde C, by a calculus of 'fractions', and prove that \tilde C is equivalent to the localization W^{-1}C.

(1) What a morphism of \tilde C is. A morphism x -> y is represented by what Grothendieck calls a 'fantaisiste' (a 'fanciful' arrow). This is a cospan x --f_0--> \bar y <--i-- y, where:
- f_0 is a cofibration;
- i is a weak equivalence (a section);
- i admits a retraction α: \bar y -> y, with α ∈ W and α i = 1_y.
We write it as [f_0, i], informally 'i^{-1} f_0'. Such representatives form a category Ch_0(x,y). The morphisms of \tilde C are presumably its connected components π_0 Ch_0(x,y).

(2) The functor \tilde C -> W^{-1}C. On objects it is the identity; it sends [f_0, i] to (image of i)^{-1} ∘ f_0. A weak equivalence f: x -> y gives two elements:
- F = [f], the image of f itself;
- G = [1_y, f], playing the role of f^{-1}.
The page sets up checking that the composites GF and FG are identities, using the definition of '=' in \tilde C. The left margin notes that the functors are bijective on objects and surjective on arrows, which reduces the comparison to checking that W becomes invertible.

(3) The functor C -> \tilde C, flagged as 'un peu plus délicat'. Given f: x -> y, choose a factorization f = α f' with:
- f': x -> \tilde y a cofibration;
- α: \tilde y -> y a weak equivalence that is a retraction, with a section i.
This is Ken Brown's factorization lemma (any map is a cofibration followed by a retraction of a trivial cofibration). Send f to [f', i]. One must show the class does not depend on the choice. Grothendieck's argument is that two such factorizations α f_0 and α' f_0' are dominated by a third one α'' f_0'', so they lie in the same connected component of Ch_0(x,y).

(4) The next page carries out this domination. It uses x ⊔ x -> y' ⊔ y'' and gluings along x of the form y' ∨_x y'' (pushouts), plus the codiagonal. This is the standard 'common refinement of two factorizations' argument.

In modern terms, the page proves that the homotopy category of a cofibration category has morphisms given by connected components of a category of left fractions (cospans) x -> \bar y <-~ y.
errors: No outright error is visible. Hypotheses are left implicit: cofibrancy of objects (the page says '(et y ... cofibrant?)'), the existence of pushouts along cofibrations, and the existence of factorizations. Without these, factorizations and the gluing on the next page are not available.

Composition in \tilde C is not defined on this page; it needs pushouts of cofibrations along trivial cofibrations. Well-definedness of composition on connected components is likewise not addressed here.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but standard reconstruction of the fraction description of the homotopy category of a cofibration category, as done by Brown in 1973. Its interest is mainly historical: Grothendieck was independently redoing abstract homotopy theory in 1982, with private terminology ('fantaisiste', Ch_0(x,y)). Nothing here appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2 likely reads '... qui se comportent comme ... On a bien des foncteurs' (with 'des' struck out); the struck word before \tilde C is illegible.
'[...] de ces deux foncteurs transforment [...] W en flèches inversibles' is probably '(les composés) de ces deux foncteurs transforment les flèches de W en flèches inversibles'.
Left margin reads roughly: 'Les foncteurs bijectifs sur les objets, surjectifs sur les flèches, ... il suffit pour le voir ... [f] ...'.
In the diagram, the dotted arc labelled β runs from y back to \bar y. It is the section i of α (the text says 'où β une section i'), so β and i denote the same map.
The bottom-left margin probably concerns 'Une fantaisiste f = [α f_0, ...] et α ∈ W, telles que α soit une rétraction / admette une section'.
